title: Bijective Counting, Stars & Bars, PIE & Pigeonhole

sections.heading: Bijective Counting, Stars & Bars, PIE & Pigeonhole Practice Exercises

questions.q: How many ordered \( 3 \)-tuples of integers \( (x_1, \dots, x_{3}) \) satisfy \( x_1 + \dots + x_{3} = 9 \) subject to \( x_i \ge 1 \) for every \( i = 1, \dots, 3 \)?
questions.answer: Shift variables by \( y_i = x_i - 1 \ge 0 \). Then \( y_1 + \dots + y_{3} = 9 - 3(1) = 6 \). By Stars and Bars, the number of non-negative integer solutions is \( \binom{6 + 3 - 1}{3 - 1} = \binom{8}{2} = 28 \).

questions.q: How many ordered \( 4 \)-tuples of integers \( (x_1, \dots, x_{4}) \) satisfy \( x_1 + \dots + x_{4} = 15 \) subject to \( x_i \ge 2 \) for every \( i = 1, \dots, 4 \)?
questions.answer: Shift variables by \( y_i = x_i - 2 \ge 0 \). Then \( y_1 + \dots + y_{4} = 15 - 4(2) = 7 \). By Stars and Bars, the number of non-negative integer solutions is \( \binom{7 + 4 - 1}{4 - 1} = \binom{10}{3} = 120 \).

questions.q: How many ordered \( 5 \)-tuples of integers \( (x_1, \dots, x_{5}) \) satisfy \( x_1 + \dots + x_{5} = 13 \) subject to \( x_i \ge 1 \) for every \( i = 1, \dots, 5 \)?
questions.answer: Shift variables by \( y_i = x_i - 1 \ge 0 \). Then \( y_1 + \dots + y_{5} = 13 - 5(1) = 8 \). By Stars and Bars, the number of non-negative integer solutions is \( \binom{8 + 5 - 1}{5 - 1} = \binom{12}{4} = 495 \).

questions.q: How many ordered \( 3 \)-tuples of integers \( (x_1, \dots, x_{3}) \) satisfy \( x_1 + \dots + x_{3} = 15 \) subject to \( x_i \ge 2 \) for every \( i = 1, \dots, 3 \)?
questions.answer: Shift variables by \( y_i = x_i - 2 \ge 0 \). Then \( y_1 + \dots + y_{3} = 15 - 3(2) = 9 \). By Stars and Bars, the number of non-negative integer solutions is \( \binom{9 + 3 - 1}{3 - 1} = \binom{11}{2} = 55 \).

Using Burnside's Orbit-Counting Lemma, how many rotationally distinct necklaces of \( 6 \) beads can be formed using up to \( 2 \) colors (where two necklaces are identical if one is a rotation of the other, without flipping)?
questions.answer: Under the cyclic rotation group \( C_{6} \), rotation by \( k \) steps decomposes into \( \gcd(6, k) \) cycles, fixing \( 2^{\gcd(6, k)} \) colorings. Grouping by \( d = \gcd(6, k) \mid 6 \) via Burnside's Lemma gives \( \frac{1}{6}\sum_{d \mid 6} \varphi(6/d)\cdot 2^d = \frac{84}{6} = 14 \).
